identity.title: The ALMA-PILS survey: first detection of methyl isocyanide (CH<SUB>3</SUB>NC) in a solar-type protostar

paper_type_evidence.quote: The observations presented here were taken as part of the PILS program, an ALMA observing program to study IRAS 16293 in Band 7, between 329.147 GHz and 362.896 GHz.
We use ALMA observations from the Protostellar Interferometric Line Survey (PILS) to search for methyl isocyanide and compare its abundance with that of its isomer methyl cyanide.

findings_qualitative.value: CH3NC is detected for the first time in a solar-type protostar, in IRAS 16293B; no lines are detected toward A

evidence.quote: No lines are detected towards the offset position of IRAS 16293A.

findings_qualitative.value: Source A and B show significant chemical differentiation, with B's ratio far lower than A's

evidence.quote: The lack of detection of methyl isocyanide in the second component in the IRAS 16293 binary, IRAS 16293A, shows that there is significant chemical differentiation between these sources.

findings_qualitative.value: CH3NC spatial morphology follows the disk component of B and resembles CH3CN

evidence.quote: The emission traces the disk component of IRAS 16293B and shows a similar morphology and extent to methyl cyanide emission.

findings_qualitative.value: Gas-phase destruction of CH3NC by H not acting on CH3CN is needed to reproduce the observed ratios

evidence.quote: The chemical modelling of methyl isocyanide has also shown that the gas-phase destruction mechanism, H+CH$_3$NC, is necessary to increase the CH$_3$CN/CH$_3$NC ratio

claims.hypothesis: Methyl isocyanide can be detected in a solar-type protostar
claims.experiment: Search for CH3NC lines in PILS ALMA spectra at offset positions toward A and B, matched to CDMS-based LTE predictions
claims.result: 10 unblended and 6 blended CH3NC lines above 3σ in B; no lines in A
claims.finding: First detection of CH3NC in a solar-type protostar (IRAS 16293B)

evidence.quote: We detect methyl isocyanide for the first time in a solar-type protostar, IRAS 16293–2422 B, and present upper limits for its companion protostar, IRAS 16293–2422 A.

claims.hypothesis: CH3CN/CH3NC abundance ratio differs between the two binary components
claims.experiment: LTE column density fits in B and 3σ upper limit in A, combined with CH3CN column densities from Calcutt et al. 2018
claims.result: Ratio of 200 in B and >5517 in A (abstract); Table 2 gives >5317 for A
claims.finding: Abundance ratio is much lower in B than in A

evidence.quote: with a CH$_3$CN/CH$_3$NC abundance ratio of 200 in IRAS 16293–2422 B and \>5517 in IRAS 16293–2422 A

claims.hypothesis: Chemical models can reproduce the observed CH3CN/CH3NC ratios in both sources
claims.experiment: Two MAGICKAL single-point models with final densities 6×10^10 and 1.6×10^7 cm^-3
claims.result: Low-density model gives ratio ~450 near B value; high-density model gives ~2.5×10^6, consistent with A upper limit
claims.finding: Model does not match B at the density representative of B; consistent with A upper limits; final density controls the ratio

evidence.quote: The chemical modelling is unable to match the observed CH$_3$CN/CH$_3$NC abundance ratio towards the B source at densities representative of that source.

claims.hypothesis: A gas-phase destruction of CH3NC by H that does not destroy CH3CN is required
claims.experiment: Rerun of models with the gas-phase and grain-surface H + CH3NC reactions switched off separately
claims.result: Disabling the gas-phase reaction moves the ratio close to unity at higher temperatures; grain-surface reaction has practically no effect
claims.finding: An efficient gas-phase destruction mechanism for CH3NC not operating on CH3CN is needed

evidence.quote: This result shows that there needs to be some efficient mechanism for destruction of CH$_3$NC in the gas-phase that doesn’t operate on CH$_3$CN.

why_this_data.value: High-sensitivity ALMA PILS data are needed because CH3NC emission is very weak in known sources

evidence.quote: high sensitivity observations are needed as it has shown very weak emission in the objects it has been detected in so far.

why_this_method.value: Source A lines are broad, so a second position near B was chosen to limit line blending

evidence.quote: The FWHM of lines around source A are much broader ($\sim$2$-$3 km s$^{-1}$) than around source B ($\sim$1 km s$^{-1}$) making line blending a significant problem

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Radiative association of CH3+ with HNC added to the model; did not significantly change CH3CN and only modestly changed CH3NC in the low-density model

evidence.quote: it was observed that the inclusion of this process did not affect the abundance of CH$_{3}$CN in any significant way

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Searching closer to the A peak continuum position; abandoned due to blending

evidence.quote: We additionally searched positions closer to the A peak continuum position, however, no lines could be identified as blending became too severe.

limitations_admitted.value: Many uncertainties in formation and destruction pathways; initial models not expected to reproduce observations

evidence.quote: There are many uncertainties in the formation and destruction pathways of methyl isocyanide, and it is therefore not surprising that the initial modeling attempts do not reproduce observations.

limitations_admitted.value: The H + CH3NC reaction is speculative with a large uncertainty on its barrier

evidence.quote: In particular, there is a large uncertainty on the barrier of the CH$_3$NC+H reaction as it likely does not equal the barrier on the HNC+H reaction.

referee_caveats_inferred: Abstract gives >5517 for source A while Table 2 gives >5317; the reproducer must choose one value
Upper-limit calculation depends on an assumed FWHM (2.2 km/s) and Tex (150 K) borrowed from other work, not measured in A
Only two spectral positions are analysed, so the B and A ratios rest on one position each
Chemical model is single-point with uniform density and an uncertain H + CH3NC barrier, so ratio conclusions are model-dependent
Column density errors are described qualitatively ('minimum change ... significant difference') without a stated threshold
